messages:
acme_sre: hey @trevor_support — after last Thursday's key rotation we see missing HSM audit entries for CloudHSM-backed keys in our prod namespace. Signing requests intermittently return 403 'Key not found' and some requests spike to 1.2s. Payment auths are failing in ~0.5% of trafffic. Happening since 2026-02-15 03:10Z. Repro steps below.

acme_sre: repro (short): 1) call POST /v1/sign with key_id=proj-prod-hsm-01 2) sometimes get 403 with body: {"error":"Key not found"} 3) repeat 10x -> 2-3 failures. Happens across multiple hosts and regions.

trevor_support: on it. Can you paste one raw request ID and the approximate timestamp (UTC)? Also which environment: "private-onprem" vs "cloud-hsm"? :eyes:

acme_sre: request_id: r-0a7c9b2f, timestamp: 2026-02-15T03:12:17Z. This is our on-prem HSM gateway talking to a CloudHSM cluster (hybrid). Cluster serial: cl-04b2f. Keys were rotated using our automation (calls to Redwood Private API).

sophie_security: tagging compliance — we need audit log ranges for those keys 2026-02-15 03:00->03:30Z. If audit records are missing that could be a retention/overwrite issue. @maria_ops can you check HSM audit buffer metrics and ingestion?

maria_ops: quick q — were keys imported with exportable=false and persistent=true? Also did the rotation script call "rotate-key" or create+expire? small differences matter for CloudHSM.

acme_sre: keys were non-exportable (exportable=false). Rotation flow: create new key -> promote -> deprecate old -> call /v1/kms/rotate (Redwood Private). We didn't explicitly set persistence flags in the call (using our infra library).

trevor_support: can you paste the HSM gateway logs around that request id? A short tail of journalctl -u hsm-gateway from 03:10->03:15 would help. Also need the KMS call ID from Redwood (x-request-id header) if available.

acme_sre: pasted logs snippet below:

```
Feb 15 03:12:16 hsm-gw[2345]: INFO request incoming id=r-0a7c9b2f key=proj-prod-hsm-01 op=sign
Feb 15 03:12:16 hsm-gw[2345]: ERR HSM_SESSION_EXPIRED cluster=cl-04b2f sess=12
Feb 15 03:12:16 hsm-gw[2345]: WARN audit-buffer: head=124560 tail=124320 retention=240s overwritten=1
Feb 15 03:12:17 hsm-gw[2345]: INFO fallback to cached-key key=proj-prod-hsm-01 result=403
```

acme_sre: also saw repeated "audit-buffer overwritten" lines earlier that morning.

maria_ops: that ERR + audit overwrite suggests the HSM session pool is exhausting and audit buffer wrap is happening. For CloudHSM we sometimes see short-lived session churn if provisioning spikes during rotation windows. Please run the following on the gateway host and paste output: 

```
sudo /opt/hsm/tools/hsm-health-check --cluster cl-04b2f --window 10m
journalctl -u hsm-gateway --since "2026-02-15 03:05" --until "2026-02-15 03:20" | sed -n '1,200p'
```

deploy-bot: Rotation job rota-2026-02-15-03 completed exit=0 duration=18s (job-id rota-2026-02-15-03)

trevor_support: thanks. Two immediate asks: 1) run hsm-health-check and share output, 2) increase gateway HSM session timeout to 120s temporarily and verify. We'll also open a vendor escalation if logs show session lease failures.

acme_sre: ran hsm-health-check output (trimmed):

```
HSM health: cluster cl-04b2f
sessions_active: 95
sessions_max: 100
session_failures: 12 (last 15m)
audit_buffer_usage: 98% (wraps: 3 in last 1h)
latency_sign_ms_p95: 820
```

acme_sre: I bumped session timeout to 120s per your suggestion, restarted hsm-gateway. Preliminary results: sign latency improved for a while but we still see a couple 403s. One more log line included:

```
Feb 15 03:18:42 hsm-gw[2345]: ERROR audit-ingest: s3_put_failed code=SlowDown bucket=redwood-audit-prod
```

sophie_security: that S3 SlowDown is concerning for audit retention exporting. If audit files fail to persist quickly the gateway will overwrite local buffers. Need to confirm exports are succeeding — can you check S3 error logs and retry policy? This has compliance implications.

trevor_support: agreed. Next steps from our side: we'll open a vendor ticket for CloudHSM (session failures + audit buffer wrap), escalate to infra for S3 SlowDown retries, and coordinate a joint call with your SREs. Can you also confirm whether any billing or quota actions ran around 03:00 that could throttle S3?

acme_sre: no scheduled billing changes. We did have a large snapshot ingestion job to S3 at 02:55 that might have throttled throughput. We'll check with infra.

maria_ops: for mitigation: 1) throttle rotation window, stagger key ops 2) temporarily increase local audit buffer (if supported) 3) add exponential retry for S3 puts with jitter 4) add health-check alert on session_failures>5. I'll post a short patch for gateway config after the call.

trevor_support: creating internal ticket and vendor escalation now. We'll include logs you pasted, health-check output, and the S3 SlowDown trace. ETA for vendor ack: ~2 hours. Planning a 1-hour bridge at 2026-02-15T16:00Z — is that ok for you?

acme_sre: yes that works. appreciate the quick triage. Please mark as P1 — payment flows impacted.

sophie_security: recording this as a compliance incident (INC-2026-02-HSM-01). We need exported audit slices for 30d retention and to confirm no missing signing events for legal. Keep me in the loop.

trevor_support: noted. I'll follow up in the ticket with vendor response and a runbook for mitigation (session pool tuning + S3 backoff). :thumbsup:

acme_sre: thanks everyone. We'll prepare network traces and S3 request IDs for the bridge.
